transcript.text: kettle keeps tripin the electrics, whole kitchen goes off. not evry time maybe 1 in 4. is it the kettle or the fusebox?? need my tea lol

It's almost always the kettle, but here's how to know for sure.

## Quick test (5 minutes)
1. Use the kettle in a different room (e.g. a lounge or bedroom socket) a few times.
• Trips there too → it's the kettle.
• Never trips there → could be the kitchen circuit or a different appliance.
2. Run something else high-power in the kitchen socket (toaster, iron, microwave).
• Those work fine every time → points back to the kettle.

## Check what's tripping at the fusebox
• RCD (wider switch, usually has a "T" or "Test" button). This trips on earth leakage, a tiny bit of current escaping where it shouldn't. Classic kettle fault.
• MCB (narrow switch labelled with a number like B32). This trips on overload, too much on at once.

## Why kettles do this intermittently
• Element breaking down with age or limescale, so it leaks current sometimes
• Water getting into the base or connector from overfilling, spills, or filling it while it's on the base
• Overload: a kettle pulls about 3kW, so if it trips only when the microwave, toaster, or washing machine is also on, that explains the "1 in 4"

## What to do
• If it's the kettle: bin it. It's not worth repairing, and new ones are £15–30. Don't keep using it, since a leaking element is a shock risk. Make sure the base is dry and you're not overfilling.
• If other things trip it too, or it trips with nothing on: get an electrician to look at the circuit or consumer unit.
• Never tape, hold, or bypass a breaker that keeps tripping. It's doing its job.

Meanwhile, a pan on the hob works for tea in an emergency ☕
